title: Manual blending with trapezoidal warp and horizon correction for cave-frame pair (Saudi 1-3)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time in source metadata; transcript content does not confirm date

locations.name: cave environment (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript references "type of cave environment here" around 00:01:46

summary: The video demonstrates a manual two-frame blending workflow for a cave interior scene when automatic stitching tools fail or produce distorted results. The presenter notes that Photoshop alone may not stitch the pair, suggesting manual warping and alignment to control perspective distortion. Color and exposure differences caused by sunlight entering the lens are addressed by reducing red and yellow and lowering luminance to harmonize the two frames. A horizon tilt is corrected before applying a trapezoidal-warp approach to align the frames, using an overlay technique to compare alignment. With the warp set (around a 25-degree edge distortion common to wide-angle lenses), the top and bottom portions are blended by hand using typical brush/erase tools to create a seamless composite.

sections.title: Initial assessment: stitching feasibility, color differences, and sun-induced color shifts
concepts: color and exposure differences due to sun entering the lens
sections.description: The speaker notes that Photoshop will not stitch the frames, mentions PtGui as an option but emphasizes distortion control via warping and manual alignment, and discusses how sun-induced color changes require downstream adjustments to match two otherwise similar exposures (noting red and yellow hues and overall luminance differences).

sections.title: Horizon correction and trapezoid distortion awareness
sections.description: The presenter identifies a horizon tilt caused by shifting and explains straightening the horizon before warping. He introduces the idea of trapezoidal distortion as a key alignment issue and discusses using an overlay between layers to preview alignment while working with the two frames.

sections.title: Warp implementation, edge correction, and manual blending workflow
concepts: manual blending with brush and eraser
sections.description: The workflow moves from comparing alignments with an overlay to applying a trapezoidal warp (approximately 25 degrees on the edges for wide-angle distortion). The top and bottom sections are aligned separately, the image size is adjusted, and a straightforward manual blend is performed. The narrator demonstrates erasing mistakes and repainting to refine the seam, illustrating a hands-on, non-automatic approach to build the final composite.
